# rrr01: reuse a retreat rank and guard its final movement epoch

Prepared for review; do not submit from this document alone.

Parent/base commit `2f0f534e8311ee597e516b11c2afca1bbf608060`, base bot
`leader_party_tuned`. Work only in `bots/pi_retreat-rank-reuse-01/` and write
IMPLEMENTATION.md. This is independent of bwa/bss, sdw, pts, reset/combat and
dead-camp progress experiments. No composition, full observation rewrite,
threat capture/cache, new loop or numeric budget/health threshold.

## Evidence and falsifiable hypothesis

Original `retreat` first attempts `move_to(spawn,true,...)`; if it cannot move and
the budget is current and self can move, it ranks ordinary reachable candidates.
The original source is:

```cpp
auto rank=[&](vec2 p){int nearest=1000;for(auto& e:s.foes)nearest=std::min(nearest,cheb(p,e.position()));return std::tuple{incoming_at(p,s.foes),-nearest,cheb(p,spawn.front())};};
auto best=s.pos;auto score=rank(best);
for(auto p:s.blocked.reachable_tiles(s.pos,1).positions()) if(rank(p)<score){best=p;score=rank(p);}
if(best!=s.pos) {bool moved=move_checked(best);invalidate_observations();return moved;}return false;
```

With N iterator candidates and I improvements, rank runs1+N+I times. Each rank
loads nearest-enemy positions and calls `incoming_at`, which reloads visible
camps and their state/geometry. At a fixed state the second evaluation on an
improvement supplies the same tuple as the comparison already computed.

SDK accounting from existing local replay states gives a representative saved
rank cost of51–152 entity/enumeration imports. Example original Swirl Heart1644
sees26 camps, no enemies, and at least six rank evaluations are needed before
improvement reranks. A one-time numeric capture could save more but needs a new
freshness/lifetime contract. This job deliberately tests scalar reuse first.
These are local input/query counts, not measured game fuel savings.

Existing native research byte-extracts incoming/camp-hit/safe-mask/rank bodies
and passes19,040 fixed-state equivalence assertions; it is not a test of this
candidate. Earlier pts01 and sdw01 demonstrate that changed query schedules can
change release actions and lose games despite locally sensible logic.

Hypothesis: remove duplicate improving-candidate evaluation while preserving
the same current-epoch chosen neighbor, and prevent a fallback movement commit
if ranking crossed rounds. Reduced duplicate work may help retreat timeliness;
no performance or strength improvement is assumed.

## Exact production change

Only `src/navigation.cpp::retreat` production code may change:

1. In the existing candidate loop compute `const auto candidate_score=rank(p)`
   once. Compare `candidate_score<score`. On improvement assign `best=p` and
   `score=candidate_score`. Keep the same iterator/expression and iteration order.
2. Inside the existing `if(best!=s.pos)` branch, immediately before the existing
   `move_checked(best)`, add exactly one current-round check:
   `if(!budget.current())return false;`.

Keep the rank lambda and its tuple order `(incoming,-nearestEnemy,spawnDistance)`
byte-identical. Keep origin's initial rank, strict comparison, tie behaviour,
candidate radius/blocked board and spawn.front unchanged. If iterator includes
origin, rank that candidate once like every other candidate; do not special-case
it away. Keep the initial safe move attempt and early returns unchanged.

The guard is an explicit behaviour boundary: stale ranking must not execute an
old-round fallback move. It is not a claim of cross-round equivalence. No guard
is needed on the final no-move return, and no per-candidate/per-getter round or
fuel queries are added. No new reserve/admission threshold, retries, extra field,
manual end_turn, exception handling or additional action attempt.

Preserve `move_checked`, including can_move and movement-restriction checks,
rejected-move handling, and all existing invalidation calls. Preserve Memory
updates in the initial safe attempt. On the new stale-return path there is no
additional Memory mutation or fallback move; do not roll back earlier mutations.
The function retains its existing boolean API and callers unchanged.

## Observation and lifetime boundary

The new tuple is an owned scalar local, not a reference into Snapshot. Do not
store SDK handles/tuples in Memory or static storage. There is no intentional
mutation or observe refresh in the existing rank loop; use the same live getters
and existing Snapshot reference. Do not recollect visibility or refresh the
blocked board after the initial safe attempt, because that would change the
decision inputs beyond this experiment. Existing invalidation/alias semantics
remain; this job does not claim to repair the full observation cache.

If a getter throws, preserve exception propagation. If a getter rolls into a new
round, the final guard prevents the fallback move. Finite ranking may finish
before that check; do not add new polling or continue with a synthetic zero-risk
result. A changed fuel schedule can change optional later work, so release
identity outside the fixed-state comparison is not a requirement or promise.

## Native public-retreat checks before PC games

Exercise the actual returned `retreat` body, production rank expression,
`incoming_at` and `move_checked`; byte extraction or linking is acceptable, but
copied ranking/dispatch expressions are not. Use scripted observation/geometry/
safe-move boundaries and identify all substitutions. Compare against the exact
original parent body on identical fixed inputs.

- Ordered candidates with multiple improvements: initial rank once plus exactly
  one per iterator element for candidate, versus original1+N+I. Instrument
  incoming/camp enumeration calls to establish counts; do not infer fuel from
  them. Include an iterator that returns origin and retain that evaluation.
- A valid simple two-improvement arrangement: self(3,3), positive awake camps
  at(4,3),range1,strength20 and(3,4),range1,strength60. Origin incoming80;
  legal neighbors(2,3) and(2,2) have60 then0. Order them to create two improvements.
  Use a failed initial safe path, physical blockers consistent with these tiles,
  and a nonempty spawn region. Assert same final movement destination.
- Separate ties, no improvement, no enemies, mixed enemy/camp risk, fractional
  strengths, nearest-enemy tie breaker and final spawn-distance tie breaker.
  Preserve float addition and candidate order; do not sort inputs to help a test.
- Safe initial move succeeds: no fallback ranking or new guard. Initial attempt
  returns wait/deferred/no-route as appropriate; existing current/can_move early
  exits remain. Empty spawn and no-neighbor cases retain their old result.
- Inject round change during origin ranking and during a later candidate getter.
  When an old-round best would otherwise move, candidate returns false with no
  move attempt and no additional Memory mutation. Compare Memory against the
  state **after** the scripted initial safe attempt, since that attempt may
  legitimately update blocked counters. Parent unsafe stale actions are not an
  expected behaviour to preserve.
- Current epoch with movement unavailable or move restriction: actual move_checked
  must block mutation. Rejected/failed movement preserves original exception and
  invalidation behaviour. Do not bypass helper checks in the fixture.
- Visibility getter failure propagates as before, not as empty danger or success.

Report exact counts and test outcomes, source extraction provenance and mock
limitations. Run SDK syntax checks for all returned production sources and
inherited relevant tests. Keep release logs/instrumentation unchanged. PC owns
release builds and games.

## Frozen PC evaluation

Review exact returned source/tests, then standard80 original-champion screen on
the existing engine3/CLI5 frozen maps/opponents/both sides. Compare to original,
not a rejected parent. Mandatory gates: zero VM faults; direct>=9/16;
common>=35/64 (original33); common banking>=44512; common gem loss<=2352
(original2139); common deaths<=548 (original498). Every missed gate means no
expansion. Record/investigate new repeated caught SDK errors separately.

Report fuel suspensions, early noninitial pauses, actor-round-normalized rates,
scores, collected/banked/lost resources and deaths. No guessed fuel-saving
threshold is added. Query-count reduction is a native mechanism result, not a
release performance gate or strength claim.

Use the already included Swirl/C02 A+B release replays for a first-action
comparison against original. Locate the earliest action/fuel divergence and
inspect its actual local observations, then the first affected retreat episode.
Distinguish safe move success, fallback ranking, actions before rollover and
empty following turns. Existing original A Heart1630–1647 provides a bounded
reference with failed safe movement and carrier exposure; earlier divergence
may mean its exact timestamps no longer recur. Do not manufacture a private
callsite or demand repetition of a stale unsafe parent move. If an observed
regression has no understood local explanation, no broad expansion until audited.

Freeze any broad/confirmation stage separately. No duplicate baseline games,
online challenge, upload or ranked change follows from this job. The ordinary
confirmation maps have already been consumed; do not relabel them fresh.

IMPLEMENTATION.md must identify exact files, tests run and outcomes, remaining
uncertainty, changes from the requested contract and any scope blocker. Do not
silently add threat caching or combine another experiment.
